# Results — Study 758 (TSA-Throughput)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The alt-data nowcasting
folklore — **accelerating TSA checkpoint throughput calls a travel-stock tailwind you can
trade early** — tested on a monthly **TSA throughput** tape (a hardcoded, LABELLED PROXY
snapshot of TSA's public daily checkpoint numbers, since the TSA site is firewalled in this
build) against a month-end **travel basket** (½ airlines `JETS` · ½ hotels `MAR`+`HLT`,
yfinance, total-return adjusted) with **SPY** as the market control. We split forward
1/3/6/12-month basket returns into months when TSA momentum is **accelerating** vs
**decelerating**, compare each to the unconditional base rate, and add a Welch *t*, a placebo
null, a market-beta control, a lead/lag scan and a tradable timing overlay. Offline &
deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| TSA tape | TSA checkpoint travel numbers — average daily throughput (millions); **hardcoded monthly snapshot**, LABELLED PROXY, as-of **2026-06-30** |
| Basket tape | yfinance daily **JETS/MAR/HLT** adjusted close (total-return adjusted); equal-weight ½ airlines · ½ hotels, month-end sampled |
| Market control | yfinance daily **SPY** adjusted close (total-return adjusted), month-end sampled |
| Window | 2019-01-31 → 2026-06-30 (**90** months; **7.4** years) |
| Signal | TSA momentum = throughput vs **12 months** prior (YoY, neutralises the travel season); **ACCELERATING** when > 0 |
| Entry / costs | **1-month execution lag** (act on the next month-end close); 10 bps one-way per switch; shorts pay 100 bps/yr borrow |

> **Snapshot caveat (named on the Signal axis).** TSA's site is firewalled here, so the
> throughput series is a hardcoded monthly snapshot of the average daily checkpoint count —
> public, widely-reported, and rounded to a **LABELLED PROXY**, not a real-tape banner. The
> famous **COVID-2020 collapse** (daily throughput bottomed near **0.09M** on 2020-04-14; the
> April-2020 monthly average is **0.11M**, a ~95% drop) is included faithfully and, being one
> enormous coincident regime, dominates any TSA-vs-returns association over this short
> post-2019 sample — a fact the verdict leans on, not around.

## The signal — forward basket returns when TSA is ACCELERATING vs the base rate

1-month execution lag; the base column is *all* months. The believers say ACCELERATING TSA
should lift the forward return; Welch *t* compares the ACCELERATING-set mean to the
unconditional mean (a real nowcast ⇒ **significantly positive** *t*). The placebo *p* is the
share of 20,000 random same-size month draws whose mean forward return is **at least** the
ACCELERATING set's (i.e. as bullish or more).

| horizon | n accel | accel mean | decel mean | base mean | accel up-rate | base up-rate | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | 64 | +0.86% | +2.40% | +1.28% | 58% | 59% | **−0.29** | 0.654 |
| 3-month  | 62 | +3.28% | +4.07% | +3.50% | 63% | 64% | **−0.10** | 0.560 |
| 6-month  | 59 | +6.87% | +5.99% | +6.62% | 71% | 69% | **+0.09** | 0.465 |
| 12-month | 53 | **+15.36%** | +4.38% | +11.94% | 77% | 68% | **+0.82** | 0.181 |

Read it carefully. Only at the **12-month** horizon does the folklore's direction show up
strongly (accelerating **+15.4%** vs base **+11.9%**, up-rate **77% vs 68%**) — but the gap
**never clears the significance bar**: the best Welch *t* is **+0.82** (placebo *p* = 0.18),
and at 1/3/6 months the excess is essentially zero or negative. A long-horizon tilt inside
the noise.

## The decisive test — does the TSA uptick *lead* the travel trade?

The whole pitch is **"real-time / early."** So we scan the correlation of TSA momentum at *t*
against the basket return over `[t+L, t+L+1]`. A genuine nowcast would show its strongest
*positive* correlation at a **positive** lead (TSA moves first, the travel trade follows).

| lead *L* (months) | −6 | −3 | 0 | +1 | +3 | +6 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| corr(TSA-mom, fwd basket) | **+0.32** | +0.23 | −0.10 | **−0.15** | −0.10 | −0.15 |

The strongest *positive* correlation sits at **L = −6** (and again at **L = −3**) — TSA
momentum is most associated with a travel-basket move that happened **three to six months in
its *past***. At every **positive** lead (TSA supposedly leading) the correlation is
**negative**. TSA momentum isn't a nowcast that leads the trade; it's a **coincident-to-
lagging** echo of travel equities that already re-rated. That is the core of the "nowcast? —
Not supported" stamp: the market prices the recovery *before* the checkpoints confirm it.

## Is it anything beyond market beta? — the regression control

Forward basket returns regressed on a constant, the contemporaneous forward **SPY** return,
and the ACCELERATING dummy. The basket is a **high-beta** travel bet (β ≈ 1.4 to SPY); the
question is whether the ACCEL dummy survives once market beta is removed.

| horizon | ACCEL dummy coef | dummy *t* | basket β to SPY |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | −0.32% | **−0.21** | 1.37 |
| 3-month  | +0.87% | +0.35 | 1.38 |
| 6-month  | +4.89% | +1.35 | 1.35 |
| 12-month | +21.13% | *(5.70)* | 1.49 |

At the tradable 1–3-month horizons the dummy is **insignificant** once SPY is in the
regression — the "nowcast" is just high-beta travel exposure. The 12-month dummy *t* of 5.70
is **not** to be trusted: it is computed on **overlapping** 12-month windows with classical
OLS standard errors (≈√12 inflation, ~6 independent blocks in 77 rows) — the placebo test on
that same 12-month horizon returns *p* = 0.18 full-sample, which is the honest read. Shown in
parentheses precisely so it is not mistaken for evidence.

## Tradability — the "long the travel basket when TSA accelerates" overlay

Hold the basket when TSA is accelerating, else cash (long/flat) — or short the basket
(long/short, 100 bps/yr borrow). One-month lag; 10 bps per switch, turnover one-way × NAV.
Sharpe is excess-of-zero (the cash leg earns 0 here — a conservative, labelled
simplification).

| book | ann. mean | ann. Sharpe | switches |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| buy-and-hold basket | **+15.9%** | **0.52** | — |
| overlay long/flat, gross | +3.2% | 0.12 | 4 |
| overlay long/flat, net @ 10 bps | **+3.1%** | **0.12** | 4 |
| overlay long/short, net | **−10.0%** | −0.32 | 4 |

The overlay **underperforms buy-and-hold** massively (**+3.1% vs +15.9%** net), and shorting
the decelerating leg *loses money outright* (**−10.0%/yr**). Because YoY TSA momentum was
still deeply *negative* through the sharpest reopening rallies of late-2020/2021 — when travel
stocks doubled — a "wait for TSA to accelerate" rule sits out exactly the returns it was
supposed to catch. The signal isn't merely un-extractable; acting on it **destroys** return.

## Robustness — window, threshold, and the COVID dependence

| variation | n accel | accel 12m mean | base 12m mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| momentum **k = 3** | 44 | +7.88% | +11.94% | **−0.87** | 0.842 |
| momentum **k = 6** | 44 | +10.10% | +11.94% | −0.42 | 0.672 |
| momentum **k = 12** (base, YoY) | 53 | +15.36% | +11.94% | **+0.82** | 0.181 |
| threshold **> +5%** | 47 | +12.14% | — | +0.05 | 0.481 |
| threshold **> +10%** | 28 | +5.58% | — | **−1.42** | 0.896 |

The 12-month tilt is **fragile**: it exists only for the YoY (k = 12) window and **flips
negative** for a 3-month window (*t* = −0.87) or a big-uptick threshold (> +10% → *t* = −1.42;
the largest YoY surges are the 2021 reopening tops you'd *fade*). Now the regime split:

| ex-COVID (drop Jun-2020 → May-2022), 66 months | n accel | accel mean | base mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | 40 | +1.43% | +1.63% | −0.11 | 0.559 |
| 3-month  | 38 | +6.21% | +4.81% | +0.45 | 0.299 |
| 6-month  | 35 | +12.05% | +8.27% | +1.20 | 0.106 |
| 12-month | 29 | +24.40% | +15.23% | **+2.12** | 0.015 |

Ex-COVID, the **12-month** tilt actually *clears* the bar (*t* = **2.12**, placebo *p* =
0.015) — but that is **one** horizon (1/3/6-month all fail), on **overlapping** 12-month
windows in a 5½-year post-truncation sample, and it says nothing about *timing* (the lead/lag
verdict is unchanged). A directionally-real long-horizon tilt, not a certified, tradable,
leading nowcast. That is exactly a `WEAK` signal.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic monthly TSA + basket-like series with a *planted* link (an accelerating month
*t* lifts the *t+1*-entered held return by `edge`). The detector + inference must recover a
planted edge and must **not** manufacture significance when the true edge is zero.

| planted edge (monthly) | n accel | accel 1m mean | base 1m mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no link) | 160 | +0.82% | +0.75% | **+0.10** | 0.447 |
| **+0.08** (large link) | 160 | +9.22% | +6.39% | **+3.25** | 0.000 |

With **no** planted link the test sits at *t* = +0.10 (no false positive); a large planted
link drives *t* to **+3.25**. The machinery is unbiased — so the real-tape *t* of ~+0.8
(full-sample) is exactly what an *absent-or-tiny*, regime-driven TSA→returns edge looks like
through this keyhole.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The folklore's **direction is real at long horizons** — accelerating TSA
  precedes a stronger 12-month basket return (**+15.4% vs +11.9%**, up-rate 77% vs 68%) — but
  full-sample it **fails the *t* ≥ 2 bar** (best Welch *t* = +0.82, *p* = 0.18), is fragile to
  the window (**flips negative** for k = 3 and for the biggest upticks), and clears the bar in
  exactly **one** spec (12-month ex-COVID, *t* = 2.12). Real-as-lore, weak-as-edge.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The "long travel when TSA accelerates" overlay returns
  **+3.1%/yr** (Sharpe 0.12) vs buy-and-hold **+15.9%/yr** (Sharpe 0.52); the long/short
  version **loses 10%/yr**. YoY momentum lags the reopening rallies, so acting on the signal
  **subtracts** return — nothing to allocate to.
- **Nowcast? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The lead/lag scan puts the strongest *positive* correlation at
  **L = −6 / −3** (TSA momentum *lagging* the travel trade by a quarter-to-half-year); at every
  positive lead it's **negative**. Travel equities lead the checkpoints, not the other way
  around. The whole appeal — *real-time, early* — is the part the data rejects.
